title: Hybrid reserved + scalable capacity pilot for Dedicated: slab subscription plus on-demand scale
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Enterprise customers have asked for better cost predictability for Dedicated while keeping the ability to absorb traffic spikes. Current offerings force a binary choice: large reserved commits or unpredictable overage. This ticket pilots a hybrid packaging model that pairs a predictable slab subscription (reserved baseline) with an integrated scalable add-on (on-demand GPU minutes) and an optional degraded SLA for temporary burst capacity.
description_2: Goals: 1) Reduce procurement friction by offering a lower baseline commit with an explicit, meterable top-up. 2) Keep 95th percentile latency SLO for baseline traffic; allow best-effort SLA for burst capacity at a reduced price. 3) Create telemetry and billing signals so customers can see unit economics (cost per token / GPU-minute) and route for optimizations. 4) Validate willingness-to-pay via a 6-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers.
success_metrics: - Pilot adoption: 3 customers onboarded and transacting within 6 weeks. - Cost predictability: customers report <=10% variance vs forecast for baseline usage. - Revenue impact: at least 12% higher ARR per customer vs equivalent current reserved-only deal. - Reliability: baseline SLA met >= 99.9% uptime; burst capacity available >= 95% when requested (no SLA guarantee).
proposal_summary: Introduce three named offerings: (1) Slab-Base: monthly reserved GPU slab (e.g., 4-GPU equivalent) with full SLA (gold). (2) Scale-Add: on-demand GPU-minutes purchasable per-hour at a premium, with best-effort availability and network isolation but no hard latency SLA. (3) Gold/Bronze SLA overlay: customers can pay to extend SLA to scaled capacity for a higher rate. Billing will show baseline reservation amortized per token + metered add-on. Discounts for annual prepay on slab.
pricing_matrix: Example tiers (pilot only): Slab-Base small (4-GPU equiv) $25k/mo, medium (8-GPU equiv) $45k/mo. Scale-Add on-demand: $X per GPU-minute (2x baseline unit). SLA overlay: +20% on scale-add. Note: final per-unit must be produced by finance modeling task ENG-5032.
engineering_tradeoffs: - Implementing metered add-on requires: quota accounting, real-time billing hooks, and runtime admission controls (ENG-4981). - To avoid cold-start penalties, scaled capacity will use pre-warmed standby nodes; increases cost but reduces latency. - Alternative of pure spot-backed burst (cheaper) rejected for pilot due to customer data residency and audit concerns.
ux_requirements: Console: new pricing display for combined reservation + metered usage, projected monthly spend widget, and capacity simulation. Billing: line-item breakdown and alerts when metered spend approaches thresholds. API: new SKU identifiers and soft-cap/auto-approve flags.
legal_and_compliance: Legal needs updated contract language for mixed SLA/limited-SLA windows and amended SOC2/audit SOW. Security questionnaire updates required: data-at-rest encryption for scaled nodes, customer-managed KMS options, and audit logging for burst allocations. See SQ responses draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Pilot-SQ-Responses (internal).
pilot_plan: - Week 0-1: finalize pricing per finance model (assigned: Finance/Emma Chen). - Week 2-3: engineering implements metering + soft-cap admission flow (ENG-4981). - Week 4: onboard pilot customer A (adtech), B (fintech), C (healthcare) with explicit SLAs and usage dashboards. - Week 6: collect feedback, update pricing, and present go/no-go to leadership.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may hit unexpected scale-add spend. Mitigation: enforce opt-in thresholds and billing caps; require explicit acceptance for scale-add during onboarding. Risk: runtime instability when burst is enabled. Mitigation: limit burst concurrency and enable graceful degradation routing to lower-cost model variants.
open_questions: - What exact per-GPU-minute rate preserves margin across typical workloads? (Finance) - Do sales/legal need a minimum commitment floor for pilot customers? - Should scale-add be subject to regional capacity checks or global pool? (Infra) - What SLA credits apply if baseline SLA is degraded due to misconfiguration during pilot?
